context.task: Locate and open the overdue task

scope: Initial work-queue composition at two widths and activation of the overdue task only; other controls are mocked.
label: Modern SaaS minimalism preference fit
weightProvenance: User-requested preference; weights and anchors authored for this skill, not empirically validated.

task.reason: Only the scoped overdue-row activation was probed; programmatic focus plus Enter opened the matching task. Discovery by users was not tested.

legibility.reason: Body/task text #aaa on white has calculated sRGB contrast about 2.32:1; normal-sized task labels are visibly faint.
evidence: assets/examples/saas/rendered/faint.html: body.faint color and white body background

interaction.reason: Task-row Enter activation and detail focus passed; navigation, toolbar and New task are nonfunctional mock controls, so this is not an approved working app.

adaptation.reason: Two widths have no root overflow; phone hides owner/due/sidebar and long content was not stress-tested. Full information availability remains unverified.

breakdown.label: Quiet hierarchy
breakdown.anchor: Several unrelated elements compete with the main task.
breakdown.reason: Heading, actions and content all have similarly weak emphasis; the primary action no longer stands apart.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Restore a clear action treatment and distinct readable type roles.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Restrained surfaces
breakdown.anchor: Mostly quiet surfaces with redundant card/border/depth treatments.
breakdown.reason: Nearly invisible row boundaries leave weaker grouping than the restrained version.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Use visible grouping cues where they carry meaning; do not remove every separator.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Typography-led composition
breakdown.anchor: Display-scale headings or excessive styles dominate routine work.
breakdown.reason: Small low-contrast labels create a fragile reading texture; the compact heading alone does not establish useful hierarchy.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Restore readable text roles and inspect contrast before adjusting density.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Useful density and rhythm
breakdown.anchor: Efficient rows/groups, clear internal versus external spacing, breathing room at transitions.
breakdown.reason: Four closely spaced records remain grouped and fit; this density alone does not validate their readability.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Keep comparison proximity while restoring readable control sizing.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Precise component language
breakdown.anchor: A recognizable system has repeated alignment or variant inconsistencies.
breakdown.reason: Consistent controls are present, but 22px visual button heights and faint treatments weaken their appearance as actions.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Restore clear control treatments and verify actual hit-area requirements and exceptions.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Purposeful color
breakdown.anchor: Saturated containers and competing accents dilute priority.
breakdown.reason: The Overdue distinction and primary-action contrast disappear into nearly uniform gray.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Restore semantic color and an unmistakable primary treatment without tinting all content.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Product-specific restraint
breakdown.anchor: Coherent but generic treatment with limited connection to product content.
breakdown.reason: The faded brand and content lose the deliberate neutral character of the clearer candidate.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Restore readable identity and domain text; no decorative addition is required.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.
